Hi Lena —

Quick note: Redwood is running a customer briefing track at Signal Summit (Nov 17-18 in SF) and we'd love to feature Firehose.ai for a 20-minute runtime briefing + 10 min Q&A. The goal is a short, customer-led talk focused on:

- why you chose the Redwood runtime for production inference
- concrete latency/cost improvements you’ve seen
- one short technical lesson learned and an outcome (SLO, rollout strategy, or infra win)

Logistics: 20 minutes on stage (30 min slot with Q&A), AV provided, prerecorded slide deck due two days before. We can offer travel stipend and complimentary passes. Attached is the Signal Summit speaking guide with timing and AV details.

Would you be open to this? If so, who from your team would present (you, Samir, or another engineer)? I can loop in Marissa from Customer to coordinate case study capture after the talk.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Diego Fernandez

> Thanks for the invite, we'd love to participate. High level questions before we commit:

Great — thanks Lena. To answer briefly:

- Format: customer case study / briefing (no live product demo required). We ask for 10–12 slides focusing on the problem, the approach, the concrete results, and one operational lesson.
- IP/ND A: you can keep any proprietary numbers high level (e.g., % latency reduction or token-cost direction). If you prefer, we can anonymize sensitive figures in the public slide deck.
- Redwood co-presenter: usually a customer success or PM (Marissa will join to introduce and handle Q&A).

Suggested outline for your 20 minutes:
1) 2 min intro + customer context
2) 6 min technical approach (runtime config, batching, caching patterns)
3) 6 min outcomes (latency/cost/SLAs)
4) 4 min lesson learned + quick demo slide (optional)

I'll set up a 30-minute prep call — Marissa, Neha: can you take point on the prep call and follow-up case study items? Lena/Samir: what day next week works best for a 30-min slot?

Thanks,
Diego
